  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE LA VERNE PLANNING COMMISSION
  WEDNESDAY, MAY 14,2025

  ACTION MINUTES

 REGULAR MEETING - 6:30 p.m. - Vice-Choirperson Allison called the meeting called to
 order at 6:30 p.m.
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE - Led by Vice-Chairperson Allison

 ROLL CALL  commissioner Keny chang, commissioner Jeremy conrad, commissioner
  Erin Dutfy, vice-chairperson Thomas Allison, and chairperson Jason
  Simison.

Commissioners present: Allison, Chang, Conrad, and Duffy
Absent: Simison
Advisory Staff Present: Community Development Director Eric Scherer, Associate Planner
  Parker StrinilbUow, Deputy City Attorney lvy Tsoi, and Public ll/orks Director Danny
  Wu.

MINUTES - April 9, 2025 - It was moved by Commissioner Chang and seconded by
Commissioner Conrad to approve the minutes of the April 9, 2025 meeting. The motion
carried by a 4-0 vote.

PUBLIC COMMENT - None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

Project: Case Numbers 37-25GUP - 1768 Arrow Highway, Suite 102- Conditional Use
Permit to operate a holistic health and wellness center located at 1768 Arrow Highway.
The property has a zoning designation of Arrow Corridor Specific Ptan and the froperty
lies within the Gommercia!/Manufacturing (C/M) area which requires approval of a
Conditional Use Permit for health spas

RECOMMENDATION:
staffrecommends that the Planning commission do one of thefollowing:
  1. Approve the project and direct staffto return at the next meetingwith a resolution
  approving the project based on appropriate findings, with or without conditions or
  modiJications deemed appropriate and afirm a categorical exemption from the
  Califurnia Environmental Act; or
  2. Continue the public hearing to a date certain to allow for further analysis or revisions;
  or
  3. Deny the project and direct staffto return at the next meeting with a resolution denying
  the project based on appropriate findings.

Regardless of whether the Planning Commission approves or denies the project, tt should
provide its reasoning to stafffor its decision so that the appropriate findings can be made and
incorporated into a resolution.
 Presentation: Associate Planner Stringlbllow made a presentation to the Planning Commission
going over the recommendations and staffreport.

Public Hearing: Vice-Chairperson Allison opened the public hearing. The applicant Priscilla
Ortiz was present at the meeting. Ms. Ortiz shared her background. She stated that she
previously operated her business for ten years in the City of Upland. Ms, Ortiz was unaware of
the steps to open her business in La Verne. She is currently referral based only and travels to
the homes of her clients while she prepares to open the new space. Ms. Ortiz provided photos of
the space for the Commissioners and Staff,

The Commissioners had questions regarding state licensing and the Upland location.

Ms. Ortiz stated that she has certificationsfor some of the services but there are no state
licensing requirements for the services she is providing. Ms. Ortiz also stated that she has a
seller's permit and appliedfor business license. She began her setup of the space in 2022,
setting up one room at a time but has not opened to the public.

Vice-Chairperson Allison closed the public hearing.

Commissioner Discussion: The Commissioners askedfor clarification regarding difference
between a massage CUP and health spa CUP.

Mr. Stringlfellow stated that the massage service is /ess than 20%. Mr. Scherer added that the
massage service is ancillary to the health spa and any future business in the space would have
to follow the same conditions.

Commissioner Chang asked if more conditions can be added to the CUP.

Mr. Scherer stated that more conditions can be added at the Commissioners request and be
brought back to the next meeting. He added that the CUP is still revocable if conditions are not
met orfollowed.

Vice-Chairperson Allison reopened the Public Hearing and askpd Ms. Ortiz if she was aware of
the complaints received by the City.

Ms. Ortiz was surprised by the complaints as she had never received hate from others or
complaints before.

Vice-Chairperson Allison closed the Public Hearing.

The Commisstoners discussed the highlighted conditions in the staffreport. Mr. Scherer stated
that he felt the highlighted conditions were appropriate for the business.

It was moved by Commissioner Conrad and seconded by Commissioner Duffy to return a
resolutionfor approval at the next regularly scheduled meeting, approving the project based on
the findings being met as set forth in the staff report, with the draft conditions of approval and
affirm a categorical exemptionfrom the Califurnia Environmental Act. Motion carried by a 4-0
vote.

  Proiect: Capita! lmprovement Plan tor 2025126 - The City of La Verne continues to
 prepare and adopt a Capital lmprovement Plan (GlP) as a part of the annual budget and
 to more responsibly plan for long range capital improvements

REGOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends the Planning Commission review the proposed Capital Improvement plan,
and adopt Resolution No. 1340, certifuing that the proposed Capital Improvement Plan,
  for
year (2025/26) is consistent with the adopted General Plan.

 Presentation: Mr. Scherer stated that Principal Planner Candice Bowcock is out sick. In her
 absence, Public Works Director Danny Wu made the presentation to the Planning Commission
 going over the recommendation and staff report that was part of the agenda packet.

 Public Comments: None

Commissioner Comments: Commissioner Chang had a question regardingfurniture
replacement form the list of improvements.

Mr. Scherer stated that any large item such as furniture replacement or auto purchases would
be listed. Mr. wu added that anything above $75,000 is included in the list.

It was moved by Commissioner Conrod and seconded by Commissioner Chang to approve
Resolution No. 1340, certifying that the Capital Improvement Programforfiscal year 2025/26
is consistent with the adopted General Plan. Motion carried by a 4-0 vote.

PLANNING COMMISSIONER GOII'IMENTS .

Commissioner Dufy stated that the new sign at the Old Town entrance looks great, and the
train line is really coming together.

DIRECTOR COMMENTS -

Director Scherer stated that the sign was fully funded by Metro A Line. The sign also has
electrical outlets on top for decorations. Mr. Scherer also announced that District money is
being used to purchase 27 new light pole brackets and banners to be installed in Old Town. The
banners will promote Old Town businesses.

 Mr. Scherer thanked Principal Planner Candice Bowcock and Assistant Planner Valerie Chin
for putting together the CIP list. He stated that more work was involved in this list due to the
 new polictes in the recently adopted General Plan.

Mr. Scherer stated that there is a needfor a June meetingfor an ordinance cleanup.

The Planning Commission thanked Ms. Bowcock and staff.

ADJOURNMENT - The meetingwas adjourned at 7:20 p.m.
